body:
In New York, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$3,500 to $9,320** in 2026, or $1.75 to $4.66 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in New York actually earn: a median of $28.64 an hour, 21% above the national median of $23.75.

| | New York | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.75 to $4.66 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $3,500 to $9,320 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $28.64 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## New York exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in New York |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,625 to $6,990 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $3,500 to $9,320 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $4,375 to $11,650 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $5,250 to $13,980 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in New York's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in New York's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New York-Newark-Jersey City | $29.53 | $3,584 to $9,558 |
| Buffalo-Cheektowaga | $25.64 | $3,191 to $8,509 |
| Albany-Schenectady-Troy | $24.83 | $3,109 to $8,291 |
| Rochester | $22.71 | $2,895 to $7,720 |

The gap between New York-Newark-Jersey City and Rochester is $6.82 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $689 to $1,838 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in New York

**Siding.** Vinyl siding dominates new homes in this part of the country. In the Mid-Atlantic region, which includes New York, 73% of new single-family homes started in 2025 had vinyl as the main wall material, according to NAHB. Vinyl is often left unpainted, so on a newer vinyl-sided house the job may be mostly trim, doors, porches and railings. Older homes with wood clapboard are a different job: scraping, priming and caulking can take as long as the painting.

**Weather and timing.** Winters here are too cold for exterior paint. Sherwin-Williams says the air, the surface and the paint all need to be at or above 35°F, and the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window. In practice that leaves late spring to early fall, which is also when painters are busiest. Booking in late winter for a spring start often gets you a better date, and sometimes a better price.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in New York

In New York City, painting on its own is on the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection list of work that does not need a Home Improvement Contractor license. Repairs over $200 and remodeling do need one, so a job that mixes painting with carpentry may be different. Outside the city, some counties license home improvement contractors, so check with your county consumer affairs office. Everywhere, ask for a certificate of liability insurance.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. Under EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, contractors who disturb that paint must be certified lead-safe and follow containment and cleanup steps. Ask to see the firm's certification before work starts, and expect it to add some cost.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by New York's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**New York rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $28.64 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 1.165**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in New York?

About $3,500 to $9,320 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In New York-Newark-Jersey City expect more, about $3,584 to $9,558.

### Where in New York is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, New York-Newark-Jersey City has the highest painter wages at $29.53 an hour, and Rochester the lowest at $22.71. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in New York?

Late spring to early fall, when the air and walls stay at or above 35°F and you can count on two dry days in a row. Book early: painters fill their calendars by spring.

### Do I need a licensed painter in New York?

In New York City, painting on its own is on the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection list of work that does not need a Home Improvement Contractor license. Repairs over $200 and remodeling do need one, so a job that mixes painting with carpentry may be different.
